title: Two signals, two very different answers
desc: A drawing of a running process receiving two kinds of signal from the kernel: one the runtime catches and answers with a thread dump, and one that ends the process where it stands.

steps.note: Your process is running your code, on its threads, in its own memory.
The kernel can deliver a signal to it: a number with a name, carrying nothing else.
SIGQUIT can be caught. The runtime catches it and writes out what every thread is doing.
Then the process carries on. That dump is what an ANR report is made of.
SIGKILL cannot be caught by anything. No handler can be registered for it.
The process stops between two instructions. No finally block, no shutdown hook, no onDestroy.
